Definition: from G1746; apparel (especially the outer robe):--clothing, garment, raiment.
BiblicalUsage: Endyma is clothing, the outer robe. John the Baptist's raiment was camel's hair in Matthew 3:4, and Jesus says the body is more than raiment in Matthew 6:25 and Luke 12:23, and asks why we take thought for raiment when the lilies neither toil nor spin in Matthew 6:28.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus puts clothing in its place — the body is more than what covers it, and the Father who dresses the lilies will dress me. I hold that worry about clothes is a small window into a bigger fear, and the cure is to look at what God already provides.
